hops.afterHeading: One cell, two kinds of process
hops.title: Axons that branch from a dendrite
hops.text: Textbook drawings plug the axon straight into the cell body. Many real neurons ignore that floor plan. In one study of mouse hippocampal CA1, roughly half of pyramidal neurons had an axon branching from a dendrite. The figure was 10 to 21 percent in sampled neocortex from rodents, cats, ferrets and pigs, and lower in macaques and humans. In awake mice, hippocampal cells whose axon arises from a dendrite fire far more often during ripple oscillations, and slice recordings and modeling show why: input onto that dendrite can trigger an action potential while escaping inhibition around the cell body.

sources.citation: Thome C. et al. Axon-carrying dendrites convey privileged synaptic input in hippocampal neurons. Neuron 83(6):1418-1430 (2014).
Wahle P. et al. Neocortical pyramidal neurons with axons emerging from dendrites are frequent in non-primates, but rare in monkey and human. eLife 11:e76101 (2022).
Hodapp A., Kaiser M. E. et al. Dendritic axon origin enables information gating by perisomatic inhibition in pyramidal neurons. Science 377(6613):1448-1452 (2022).

hops.title: Thirty pounds of yew bark for half a gram of taxol
hops.text: In August 1962 the botanist Arthur Barclay peeled bark from a Pacific yew in Washington's Gifford Pinchot National Forest, one of 114,000 plant samples in a National Cancer Institute drug screen. In 1964 he went back for more than 30 pounds. Chemists Monroe Wall and Mansukh Wani spent a year and a half purifying half a gram of taxol from it, a yield of about four thousandths of a percent. In 1979 and 1980 Susan Horwitz's group showed its trick: it stabilizes microtubules instead of breaking them down. Taxol chemotherapy can injure sensory nerves. In one rat experiment, low-dose taxol applied at a spinal injury helped primed sensory axons regrow.

sources.citation: Cech N. B. & Oberlies N. H. From plant to cancer drug: lessons learned from the discovery of taxol. Nat. Prod. Rep. 40(7):1153-1157 (2023).
Schiff P. B. & Horwitz S. B. Taxol stabilizes microtubules in mouse fibroblast cells. PNAS 77(3):1561-1565 (1980).
Hellal F. et al. Microtubule stabilization reduces scarring and causes axon regeneration after spinal cord injury. Science 331(6019):928-931 (2011).
Microtubule cytoskeleton dysfunction in chronic pain (review, 2026), PMC13607021.

hops.title: Why shingles often follows a band of skin
hops.text: Shingles usually causes a one-sided band of rash, sometimes decades after chickenpox. Both come from varicella-zoster virus. During chickenpox, the virus is thought to reach sensory ganglia through the bloodstream or by traveling inward from the skin along microtubules in sensory axons, and its DNA can remain dormant inside ganglion neurons. If the virus reactivates, it can travel outward along those tracks to the skin. The rash usually follows one or two neighboring sensory nerve territories.
